children: U.S. mega banks delivered a mixed performance in the third quarter, with several lenders beating Wall Street estimates even as weakness in markets-related revenue weighed on some results.
Against this backdrop, Bank of America
stands out in Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings screen, ranking first among six major U.S. banks with a Strong Buy rating of 4.72. The remaining five banks carry Hold ratings, led by Wells Fargo

Bank of America tops the list despite a sharp post-earnings selloff after a $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge dragged down its third-quarter results. The bank reported diluted earnings per share of $0.91, below the $1.09 consensus estimate and down from $1.04 a year earlier. Shares plunged 8.56% on Wednesday, marking their steepest daily decline since April 2025.

Wells Fargo ranks second with a Quant Rating of 3.45, followed by JPMorgan Chase in third place at 3.41. Wells Fargo shares traded lower after capital markets revenue fell short of expectations, weighing on overall revenue.

JPMorgan, meanwhile, missed Wall Street estimates for both earnings and revenue as commercial and investment banking results softened from the previous quarter, although all its business lines recorded year-over-year growth.
ranks fourth with a rating of 3.34, ahead of Goldman Sachs
at 3.28. Citigroup beat third-quarter earnings expectations, supported by gains in its services and wealth businesses, which offset a sequential slowdown in markets and investment banking revenue.

Goldman Sachs also exceeded consensus estimates for earnings and revenue, despite markets-related revenue easing from an unusually strong second quarter. Morgan Stanley rounds out the list after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue, with net interest income growth and gains in equity and wealth management offsetting weakness in fixed income and investment management.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and price momentum relative to their sector peers.
